This was my first introduction into the Silent Hill series, and man, was it a great one. The entire game from start to finish was amazing. The way the story played out, the enemies, the atmosphere and the soundtrack contributed to a deeply eerie game that left me unsettled the whole way through. Some nuanced aspects of the story escaped me because I was not familiar with 1960's Japanese weddings and I missed some of the diaries, but once I did a quick web search it all fell into place. 

I highly recommend this game for any fan of horror.

Overall, it's a good game, but only for a one-time playthrough. I don't plan on playing the other four endings.

I loved the aesthetics, the story, the music, and the characters. I think Silent Hill F is an excellent game, but there's one major problem: the combat system. It's awful, and for some reason, it's omnipresent all the time. I feel like I'm playing a fighting game, not a psychological horror game. And the worst part is that Hinako is so heavy to play in combat, it's a nightmare. But despite this major flaw, the game is very good in every other aspect, and I don't regret spending so much time (and money) on it.
I am not joking. When playing the finest AAA games, I sometimes feel compelled to complete them quickly. However, this game is different. I play it and hope to God it never ends. It's that fantastic.

This is my second attempt at the Silent Hill franchise, having previously played only SH2 on the PS2. Honestly, I can’t figure out how “SH purists” can’t enjoy this game.

The story is beautifully written. Hinako is such a strong main character, and her past only becomes deeper and more compelling through NG+ and NG++. It’s a really great game.

You might not like the replay factor, though. To fully understand what’s going on, you need to play the game at least three times: once for the main ending, another time to get the other three endings, and a final run for the last ending.

If you don’t enjoy this kind of replayability, download save files specifically from just before returning to the Shimizu family house, and you won’t miss about 90% of the important cutscenes.

A complete fumble. It's ultimately just an action game with a horror aesthetic, but there is no tension or fear to be found in this game. The combat is one of the most awkward systems I've experienced, and unlike other Silent Hill games where you can just choose to not engage, this game essentially forces you into combat 90% of the time anyway, ESPECIALLY the further you get into it. The otherworld segments also overstay their welcome real quick. It's a shame, because the setting and atmosphere could have been great, and the trailers leading up to this made it seem like it was going to truly be scary, but the gameplay makes it a drag. The fact you have to complete this game apparently 3.5 times to even experience the full story is crazy, because one playthrough left me exhausted. My opinion, just get the Silent Hill 2 Remake, its a better experience in every aspect.

This is my first silent hill so I don't have a preconceived notion of what a silent hill game really is. I really enjoyed this game though, the atmosphere, the soundtrack, the characters, they all were worth the price of admission for the story.

You are in tight spaces, enemies can pop up out of nowhere, the soundtrack is eerie but also beautiful at the same time. You start off feeling clunky, scared, unsure. Just exploring on its own is fun trying to find items or items that explain the backstory of the town, the gods, the characters more.

My main complaint would be that it drags on a little at the end, and the other world temple levels can be a bit repetitive. But if you can stick through it this game is very fun and haunting.

Silent Hill F requires you to play multiple endings to understand the full story which can annoy some people but I enjoyed seeing the new dialogue as I got more faith and stronger. I know these games aren't supposed to be combat oriented but man is it fun end-game to use the katana and counter, even final bosses.

I'd play it alone for the atmosphere of the town and the soundtrack, the puzzles are hard but fun I wouldn't do lost in the fog difficulty puzzles until you do the normal version of it to understand it better.

Let me just start by saying: Silent Hill F is an atmospheric, beautifully unsettling return to form… but more importantly, it has Kotoyuki, and I am absolutely, irreversibly, cosmically thrilled about that.

The story? Great. The horror? Fantastic. The music? Chilling.
But Kotoyuki? Oh, that’s the real masterpiece. Every time he appeared on screen I basically forgot the horrors around me because I was too busy grinning like an idiot. I don’t even care if the world is ending—Kotoyuki is here, and therefore everything is fine.

The monsters might be terrifying, the mysteries might be skin-crawling, but nothing gets my heart racing like the next moment where Kotoyuki shows up again. I was genuinely invested in the lore, but I was emotionally invested in Kotoyuki, and I need the developers to know they made the correct creative decision by putting him in this game.

At some point I realized I was progressing the story solely to see more Kotoyuki. If they release DLC that is just Kotoyuki reading a grocery list for 45 minutes, I will buy it instantly. Full price. Twice.

Playing as a schoolgirl that can dodge teleport, parry massive monsters and (spoilers) grow a massive bloodborne style wolf arm by triggering a devil may cry rage meter does not really feel like Silent Hill to me.

But regardless of that, I hated the dumb anime story (I know there is a lot of fans of the writer but I don't get it), forced fight moments where objective is "Kill all the monsters", dark souls like boss encounters, being stun locked by 3 monsters in a tight room, super obvious story that somehow wants you to replay it 4 times (once was more than enough for me due to terrible gameplay).

I was really looking forward to this and I really love the visuals and monster design in this one, but yeah it's a very very tedious game.

As much as I would want to like Silent Hill f for its atmosphere, designs, and exploration, the combat just ruins everything. A lot of combat game design decisions lock you into a single possible action in a lot of cases (or even doesn't give you any reasonable ways to fight), turning the combat (which is very often required to progress) into a slog. Especially this issue is prevalent on bosses.

Which is why, while finishing around 75% of the game, I don't plan to finish it. The feeling of frustration from the combat just overpowers any other emotions I have from this game.

I really enjoyed my time with Silent Hill F. Without getting into spoilers a few of the cutscenes were absolutely terrifying. I had a pretty visceral reaction. The atmosphere and scares overall were great. Boss fights felt fun. The voice acting from the main character was fantastic (I played in Japanese). The school was a cool location (as well as the whole spirit world). The overall visual presentation, especially the red flowers and white wife enemy were good. The combat felt ok, not as bad as some reviewers were saying but it definitely is much worse than SH2 Remake and all the RE Remake games combat. More melee focused which I enjoyed but it didn't feel well executed. I also really disliked the huge amount of enemies you are forced to fight in the last section of the game. Felt very forced and reusing the same boss type enemies felt repetitive. Other than that though the story and theme of the game was great. I really wish you could get a different ending on your first playthrough, the other endings I saw looked super fun and ended the story in a much better way. The one you get for completing the game the first time feels a bit out of left field and doesn't wrap up the story in a satisficing way. Overall would recommend it on sale, but I prefer SH2 Remake.
